nodes.name: Nightly 04:17
nodes.notes:
Once a night, in the quiet hour. 04:17 rather than 04:00 on purpose — every other cron on this box fires on the hour, and a database snapshot competing with them for disk is slower for no reason.

This is one of the deliberate 'go and do work' schedules, not a watcher. But unlike the daily briefings it costs NO tokens: the backup endpoint does the whole job itself. Only a FAILURE spends a turn.

Keep it inside OCTAVIUS_STALE_HOURS (default 48) or `status` will report stale on a healthy deployment.

nodes.name: Igor: back up the brain
nodes.notes:
THE WHOLE JOB, and nothing to edit. Igor snapshots the database with VACUUM INTO (consistent even though it is live and in WAL mode), runs an integrity check on the snapshot, gzips it, uploads it to the Drive folder named by OCTAVIUS_DRIVE_FOLDER, confirms the stored size, and trashes everything past OCTAVIUS_KEEP.

15-minute timeout: on a large database the snapshot and upload take real time, and a node that gives up at 30s would report a failure for a backup that then completes.

onError continueRegularOutput: the endpoint returns 200 with ok:false when a backup fails, so the Gate can tell a failed backup apart from an unreachable Igor. This covers the second case.

nodes.name: Gate
nodes.notes:
Fires on FAILURE, not on success — the work already happened upstream for free. A good night returns no items and stops here.

Edge-triggered via static data: a revoked Google token fails identically every night, and one push a night would bury the one that mattered.

nodes.name: Igor: tell Orion
nodes.notes: One agentic turn, only when the owner's protection is actually gone. The intent differs by failure stage — an integrity failure is a statement about the LIVE database and must not arrive worded like a flaky upload.
